summary: In a fiction excerpt from Book 14, the narrator Zen and Monica talk after an encounter with two police officers. Zen explains how he came to know of Godwin, who wrote a witty letter rebutting an FBI takedown notice aimed at Wikipedia over an official seal image. The two then share breakfast in a mood of defiant relief, but anxiety remains about a possible warrant. Monica mentions her weekend class and a planned evening play with Novak, and Zen hints at a secret meet-up with the Group that he decides not to disclose.
one_line: Zen and Monica discuss a police visit, Godwin's letter to the FBI, and anxieties about a possible warrant over breakfast.
key_facts: Zen says he first looked up Godwin when the FBI sent Wikipedia a takedown notice over a picture of the FBI's official seal.
Zen argues the takedown was unfair because the Encyclopaedia Britannica had the same picture in its article and was not made to remove it.
Zen says Godwin wrote a hilarious letter explaining why the FBI was legally off base.
Zen says he read Godwin's letter when he was about ten years old.
Godwin figured the best way to deal with an abuse of power is to make fun of it publicly, according to Zen.
Monica says Zen is strange, 'In a good way.'
Zen's father says people whose houses are flooded or blown down in a tornado often suddenly love their neighbors, though this usually does not last long.
Monica asks whether a judge would sign off on a warrant on a Saturday, and Zen says the authorities are calling it a terrorist investigation.
Monica describes the search as security theatre, comparing it to making people take their shoes off at airports.
Monica has a weekend college class to teach and plans to meet Novak, who wants to go to a play that night.
Zen decides not to tell Monica about his meet-up with the Group because she would worry and not understand.
Monica gets upset when Zen uses four-letter words, as if it means she is failing as his legal guardian.
